The paper investigates the magnetic properties of (Ga,Mn)N thin films in proximity to Mg-doped GaN.
The trilayer heterostructures are grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) technique.
The (Ga,Mn)N layer is sandwiched between two thicker GaN:Mg cladding layers.
The thickness of the (Ga,Mn)N layer is between 3.8 and 4.8 nm.
The concentration of Mn in the (Ga,Mn)N layer is about 5%.
The presence of neighboring GaN:Mg layers does not affect the spin-spin interactions in the central (Ga,Mn)N layer.
The lack of any effect of the adjacent Mg-doping is attributed to the presence of residual Mn in the cladding layers.
The method used to determine the Mn concentration in the (Ga,Mn)N layer is cross-section EDX measurements.
The method used to determine the Mg doping levels in the GaN:Mg cladding layers is secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS).
The range of Mg doping levels in the GaN:Mg cladding layers is from 3×10^17 cm^-3 to 9×10^20 cm^-3.
The paper uses improved-sensitivity integral SQUID magnetometry as the experimental approach.
The trilayer heterostructures are grown on fully relaxed GaN templates.
The GaN templates are fabricated by metalorganic vapor phase epitaxy (MOVPE) on c-plane Al2O3 substrates.
The radio-frequency nitrogen plasma source operating at a power of 300 W is used to grow the GaN:Mg and (Ga,Mn)N layers.
The nitrogen flux is set to 1.3 sccm.
The Ga flux is 2×10^-6 Torr BEP.
The Mn flux is 1×10^-6 Torr BEP.
The Mg flux is varied from 0 to 2×10^-8 Torr BEP.
